chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah or Burayd, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:
Allah has indeed addressed Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) in His Book. He said: I said, “In which place?”

And had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you and sought forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had sought forgiveness for them, they would surely have found Allah Ever-Relenting, Merciful.

But no, by your Lord, they do not believe until they make you judge regarding that over which they disputed among themselves, concerning what they had covenanted upon themselves: that if Allah were to cause Muḥammad to die, they would not return this matter to Banī Hāshim.
Then they should find in themselves no distress regarding what you have judged upon them, whether killing or pardon, and submit with full submission.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام) as Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: wronged themselves through sin or disobedience
key_terms.يُحَكِّمُوكَ: take you as judge and arbiter

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith interpret Qur'an 4:64-65 in relation to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a tafsir-oriented reading of Qur'an 4:64-65, stating that Allah addressed Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) in these verses. It emphasizes true faith as requiring recourse to the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in judgment, seeking forgiveness through him, and complete submission without inward resistance.
